market_context: U.S. futures point to a broad holiday rebound, with S&P 500 futures up about 1.6%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 2.2%, and Dow futures up 1.3% as semiconductor and AI shares recover (finance.yahoo.com). SPY was indicated near $728.10 and QQQ near $647.64 premarket, but the 1 p.m. ET close, light volume, restrictive Fed expectations, and tariff concerns warrant allowing for a partial fade rather than extrapolating the entire gap (unusualwhales.com, investing.com).

predictions.reasoning: SPY traded near $728.10 premarket, up 1.6%, while S&P 500 futures also gained roughly 1.6%, leaving a substantial cushion above the $716.70 baseline ([unusualwhales.com). The target assumes thin, shortened-session trading erases a small portion of the gap without reversing the broader rebound.

QQQ was indicated at $647.64, up 2.2%, as Nasdaq-100 futures surged and investors bought battered chipmakers, hyperscalers, and other AI-linked shares (unusualwhales.com, investing.com). The target retains most of that rebound while discounting holiday volatility and QQQ's 3.9% five-day decline.

Dow futures rose 1.3% and DIA was indicated at $507.98 premarket, showing that the advance extended beyond technology (finance.yahoo.com, unusualwhales.com). A close at $505.50 would surrender part of the indicated gap while still finishing comfortably above the baseline.

Premarket reports placed NVDA's gain between roughly 3% and 4.7% as investors returned to battered AI stocks, although Reuters noted that it remained more than 37% below its October record (finance.yahoo.com, investing.com). The rebound supports a close above $149.30, but ongoing AI profitability and financing concerns justify lower confidence than for the index ETFs.
